methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $11M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Vertical Semiconductor is a seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 11 peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, comprising 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and PsiQuantum.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($11M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier to step-up to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $28M. This method reflects empirical patterns in early-stage semiconductor financing where risk-adjusted step-ups approximate this magnitude between seed and Series A.

Peer-median comparison was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—the broader peer set exists but does not yield three or more datapoints at tight comparability filters, making sector-wide median analysis unreliable. The single-method triangulation produces a median valuation of $28M with a supported range of $23M to $32M. Key uncertainties include technology inflection risk inherent to frontier semiconductor plays, the absence of revenue or unit-economics data, and the wide dispersion in post-seed outcomes across the sector. Any refinement of this range would benefit from clarity on IP stage, technical team differentiation, and path to first commercial application.
